items.title: "Papa Jack" Laine, Mrs. "Papa Jack" Laine and Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1959-02-27
items.q: I know. Raymond came by that very night. He was a pretty good son of a player... I never did get to know you, son.

ctx.x: Yeah. Him and Dick Allen was at the week there. Boyk. Yeah. He liked him plenty. I never did get to know you, son.

No. I'm sorry to say, but I know. Raymond came by that very night. He was a pretty good son of a player, Johnny. Yeah, I had a boy. Swell draft player. Yeah. Swell draft player. Yeah. I'm not a player. You start to say something about your son a few minutes ago, but he never was very big or strong, really.

No, he never was, no. He didn't play all the Franks. Alfred, Alfred never was a big stride. He was always delicate, Lord. Always delicate. Always delicate. You just had one child? No, I got a daughter. Oh. Yeah, I got a daughter. And there's seven years difference between them, between Alfred and Alma. Oh. And so, Alfred, he was always sickly, all the time. But then after a long, he got a long time, and then he got diabetes, he got a stroke. And after that, he got the diabetes. And three months before he died,…

items.title: Johnny Wiggs Interview, 1969-12-14
items.q: But if they ever did play a jazz number, they could be happy for the separate reason that you take men like Harry Shields and Raymond Boyk. They're about the best right now because the other ones is deceased.
